purpose: The single description of the camera's control surface.
tools/canonscope is the contract; this file states what that contract is,
in a form a test can check. tools/tests/test-schema.py asserts three-way
agreement: every verb the dispatcher accepts appears here, every verb here
returns exactly the --json keys promised, and every MCP tool in
The MCP server does NOT build its registrations from this file. Its tools
stay as readable decorated functions with real type hints and real prose;
the test is what keeps them honest. Generating them dynamically would make
the server harder to read without making it any safer -- the drift that
actually hurts is a renamed verb or a changed key, and the test catches
Verbs with no 'mcp' block are CLI-only. A future consumer adds its own
projection block per verb, and the test grows a case.

status.summary: Camera health and current state, in one round trip.

capabilities.summary: What this body supports. Static; cacheable for a session.

shoot.summary: Take a photograph; the JPEG lands on the host, not the card.

args.name: --sv
args.description: ISO, Canon 'real' value. Omit for automatic.

args.name: --sd
args.description: Subject distance, e.g. '2m'. Omit for autofocus.

args.name: --flash
args.description: Defaults to off: firing it browned this body out at 69% battery.

preview.summary: Live-view frames. No shutter actuation, no card write.

args.name: --format
args.description: PPM needs nothing; PNG needs ImageMagick 'convert'.

zoom.summary: Move the optical zoom. 126 discrete, repeatable steps.
zoom.refuses: below 3400 mV on battery power, unless CANONSCOPE_FORCE=1

focus.summary: Fix focus at a distance, or hand it back to autofocus.

args.name: distance
args.description: A whole number of mm, or 'auto'.

focus.note: Both modes return the same keys; requested_mm is null for auto.

lua.summary: Run arbitrary Lua on the camera. The escape hatch.

args.name: code
args.description: Lua source; needs a 'return' to hand a value back.

camera_show_image.summary: Return a captured file as an image block, by path.
camera_show_image.why: The capture verbs return paths. Inlining a 4000x3000 JPEG is very token-expensive, and image blocks have been reported arriving at models as raw base64 text. Looking is a separate, deliberate act.
